summary: Iraq: Mustafa Sanad said nationwide 5G, including the Kurdistan Region, would be launched in a coordinated manner under federal spectrum allocation and a single sovereign representative.
Iraq: New official social-media signals include a 40% government internet price cut, electronic licensing, a speed-test application and CMC closures of Korek locations.
Iraq: Sanad linked 5G commercialisation with the Basra-to-Europe transit-fibre corridor, while the judicial freeze on NMTC remains a prerequisite risk.
Jordan: TRC's two 2026 priorities are mobile-number portability, scheduled for April 2027, and continued 5G expansion.
Jordan: Orange Jordan filed a routine disclosure on 24 August while the three operators remain in the implementation period for their 690-site commitments.
Lebanon: Charles Hajj's reform programme advances Law 431, TRA and Liban Telecom; more than USD 50 million was invested in the network in 2025 and first-phase fibre covers 350,000 households.
Lebanon: Hajj positions the country as an East-West digital hub through regional links with Iraq and Syria and new submarine cables; Starlink is framed as enterprise backup.
Regional: The 17 August US-Iran memorandum window has passed, while Hormuz and sanctions remain common fiscal and compliance variables for the three markets.
